inlines.text: We will need this in part b.

spec.description: Equal chords AB and CD and radii forming triangles AOB and COD. Ordinary source colours use house black.
spec.mathematics: A and C are symmetric upper circle points; B and D are symmetric lower points. AB=CD. O is the centre.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and equality ticks are permanent givens.

answer.short: $CO$; radii; $DO$; radii; SSS; $\angle COD$; matching angles in congruent triangles are equal.
answer.worked: $AB=CD$ (given), $AO=CO$ and $BO=DO$ (radii). Therefore $\triangle AOB\equiv\triangle COD$ (SSS). Hence $\angle AOB=\angle COD$ and $\angle ABO=\angle CDO$ (matching angles in congruent triangles are equal).

inlines.answer: Matching sides in congruent triangles are equal.

inlines.text: From parts a and b we can conclude that:
Chords of equal length in a circle subtend equal angles at the centre and are equidistant from the centre.

spec.description: Equal chords with perpendiculars OP and OQ, equality ticks on upper chord portions and right-angle markers. Ordinary source colours use house black.
spec.mathematics: Symmetric chords AB and CD; P and Q are the perpendicular feet from the centre O.
spec.answerVisibility: All labelled geometry and supplied markers are permanent givens.

answer.short: $\angle ODQ$; $DO$; radii; AAS; matching sides in congruent triangles are equal.
answer.worked: $\angle OPB=\angle OQD=90^\circ$ (given). Since $P$ lies on $AB$ and $Q$ lies on $CD$, part a gives $\angle OBP=\angle ODQ$. Also $BO=DO$ (radii). Therefore $\triangle OPB\equiv\triangle OQD$ (AAS), so $OP=OQ$ (matching sides in congruent triangles are equal).

inlines.text: The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

spec.description: Sloping chord AB and dashed perpendicular OP. Radii OA and OB are intentionally absent.
spec.mathematics: O is the circle centre. A and B lie on the circle. P is the perpendicular foot on chord AB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied chord, dashed perpendicular, right-angle marker, centre dot and labels are visible.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle OAP$ and $\triangle OBP$:

$$\begin{aligned}\angle OPA&=\angle OPB=90^\circ\\OA&=OB\end{aligned}$$

The angles are right angles because $OP\perp AB$, and $OA=OB$ because they are radii. Also $OP$ is common.

Therefore $\triangle OAP\equiv\triangle OBP$ (RHS). Hence $AP=PB$ (corresponding sides of congruent triangles are equal). The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.
